root_cause.summary: the fixture builds 'time' from pd.Timestamp(date(...)). Under pandas 3.0.3 that yields datetime64[s]; Parquet has no second unit, so pyarrow coerces it to timestamp[ms] on write and the re-read frame is datetime64[ms]. Only the datetime UNIT differs.

controlled_experiments.case: B same data cast to datetime64[ns]

why_the_reviewer_saw_27_27: on pandas 2.x pd.Timestamp(date(...)) is datetime64[ns], which does round-trip as ns, so the same assertion passes; the reviewer receipt was not produced natively on this host
data_correctness: no value corruption and no field loss: all twelve supplier fields are present and equal elementwise; this is a dtype-unit assertion, not a data defect

latent_production_risk.position: inside the per-batch loop, AFTER supplier.call('get_price') has already returned and AFTER the raw parquet is written
latent_production_risk.consequence_if_triggered: quota is spent, the batch parquet exists, then the run aborts; a retry would additionally hit require(not batch.exists()) -> RAW_REPLAY_COLLISION on that same batch
latent_production_risk.unknown: whether jqdatasdk 1.9.8 under pandas 3.0.3 returns 'time' as datetime64[ns] or datetime64[s] cannot be established without calling the supplier, which this task forbids while the gate fails

not_done_deliberately: did not patch the test or the script (contract forbids local patches/aliases)
did not downgrade pandas or swap the interpreter
did not run acquire_daily.py to 'see what happens'
did not touch the credential file

options_for_reviewer.description: pin the fixture to datetime64[ns] explicitly and, independently, make the production readback compare values plus normalised unit rather than exact dtype unit
keep exact-dtype intent but write with an explicit timestamp unit (e.g. coerce_timestamps='us' or cast the time column before writing) so the round trip is unit-stable
declare the required pandas major version and run the gate under it; no code change

recommendation: option A or B is needed regardless of environment, because the contract's own 'preserve original dtypes' requirement and 'verify values/dtypes on readback' requirement collide with Parquet's second-unit coercion; a pandas pin alone leaves the production line fragile
